title: The first beings
summary: First came Chaos, then broad-breasted Gaia, misty Tartarus and Eros; from Chaos came Erebus and Night.

title: Gaia bears Uranus and the Titans
summary: Gaia bears starry Uranus to cover her; lying with him she bears the twelve Titans, the Cyclopes and the Hundred-Handers.

title: Kronos castrates Uranus
summary: Uranus hides his children in the earth; Gaia makes a sickle of adamant and Kronos cuts off his father's genitals. From the blood spring the Erinyes and the Giants; from the foam, Aphrodite.

title: Kronos swallows his children
summary: Warned that a son will overthrow him, Kronos swallows each child of Rhea; she gives him a stone in swaddling clothes instead of Zeus, who is hidden in Crete.

title: Zeus frees his siblings
summary: Kronos vomits up the stone and the children; Zeus sets the stone at Pytho, frees the Cyclopes, and is given thunder and lightning.

title: The war of the Titans
summary: Ten years of war between the Olympians on Olympus and the Titans on Othrys; with the Hundred-Handers Zeus wins and the Titans are bound in Tartarus.

title: The world divided by lot
summary: The three sons of Kronos cast lots: Zeus wins the sky, Poseidon the grey sea, Hades the murky dark; the earth and Olympus are common to all.

title: Typhon
summary: Gaia's last child, the hundred-headed Typhon, challenges Zeus, who blasts him with thunderbolts and hurls him into Tartarus.

title: The war of the Giants
summary: The gods learn they can defeat the Giants only with a mortal's help, and Heracles fights beside them; Athena throws Sicily onto Enceladus.

title: The sacrifice at Mekone
summary: Prometheus divides an ox, hiding the meat in the stomach and dressing the bones in fat; Zeus chooses the fat, and so mortals burn bones for the gods.

title: The theft of fire
summary: Zeus withholds fire; Prometheus steals it in a hollow fennel stalk and gives it to mortals.

title: Pandora
summary: In return for fire Zeus has Hephaestus mould a woman from earth and the gods adorn her; Epimetheus accepts her, and she opens the jar of evils.

title: Prometheus bound
summary: Zeus binds Prometheus and sends an eagle to eat his liver, which grows back each night, until Heracles kills the eagle.

title: Deucalion's flood
summary: Zeus floods the earth; warned by Prometheus, Deucalion and Pyrrha survive in a chest, land on Parnassus, and make new people by throwing stones over their shoulders.

title: Athena is born from the head of Zeus
summary: Zeus swallows the pregnant Metis so that no son will overthrow him; Athena is born from his head, in Pindar after a blow of Hephaestus's axe.

title: The birth of Apollo and Artemis
summary: Leto wanders until barren Delos receives her; Hera keeps Eileithyia away for nine days, and Apollo is born beside the palm.

title: Apollo kills the serpent at Delphi
summary: Apollo founds his oracle under Parnassus and shoots the she-serpent there; the place is named Pytho from her rotting.

title: Hermes steals the cattle of Apollo
summary: Born at dawn, Hermes makes the lyre from a tortoise by noon and steals fifty cattle of Apollo by evening; Zeus reconciles them and Apollo takes the lyre.

title: Hades takes Persephone
summary: Hades seizes Persephone with Zeus's consent; Demeter withholds the grain until Persephone is returned for part of each year, having eaten a pomegranate seed. Demeter founds her Mysteries at Eleusis.

title: Ares and Aphrodite in Hephaestus's net
summary: Told by Helios of the affair, Hephaestus traps Ares and Aphrodite in an unbreakable net and calls the gods to see them.

title: Hephaestus thrown from Olympus
summary: Zeus throws Hephaestus from Olympus and he falls all day onto Lemnos; elsewhere Hera casts him out for being lame.

title: Athena and Poseidon contest Athens
summary: Poseidon strikes a salt spring on the Acropolis, Athena plants the olive, and the city is judged hers.

title: Arachne
summary: The weaver Arachne challenges Athena, weaves the loves of the gods, and is turned into a spider.

title: Apollo and Daphne
summary: Struck by Cupid's arrow, Apollo pursues the nymph Daphne, who is turned into a laurel.

title: Io
summary: Zeus loves Io and turns her into a cow; Hera sets hundred-eyed Argus to guard her, Hermes kills him, and a gadfly drives Io to Egypt.

title: Europa and the bull
summary: Zeus as a bull carries Europa across the sea to Crete, where she bears Minos, Sarpedon and Rhadamanthys.

title: Cadmus founds Thebes
summary: Seeking Europa, Cadmus follows a cow to the site of Thebes, kills the serpent of Ares, sows its teeth on Athena's advice, and marries Harmonia.

title: The birth of Dionysus
summary: Tricked by Hera, Semele asks to see Zeus as he is and is burned by his lightning; Zeus sews the unborn Dionysus into his thigh.

title: Pentheus
summary: King Pentheus of Thebes refuses the god's rites and is torn apart by the maenads, his mother among them.

title: Danaë and the golden rain
summary: Warned that his grandson will kill him, Acrisius shuts Danaë in a bronze chamber; Zeus comes to her as golden rain and she bears Perseus.

title: Perseus beheads Medusa
summary: With gifts from the gods and guided by Athena, Perseus cuts off Medusa's head while looking at her reflection; Pegasus and Chrysaor spring from her neck.

title: Perseus rescues Andromeda
summary: Cassiopeia boasts that she is fairer than the Nereids, and Andromeda is exposed to a sea monster; Perseus kills it and marries her.

title: The birth of Heracles
summary: Zeus swears that the descendant of his born that day will rule; Hera delays Alcmene's labour so that Eurystheus is born first.

title: The infant Heracles strangles the serpents
summary: Hera sends two serpents to the cradle; the infant Heracles strangles them.

title: The madness of Heracles
summary: Driven mad by Hera, Heracles kills his children by Megara. In Apollodorus the Pythia then sends him to serve Eurystheus for twelve years and perform ten labours; in Euripides the madness comes after the labours, and Megara dies too.

title: The Nemean lion
summary: The lion, born of Typhon, cannot be wounded, so Heracles chokes it and carries it to Mycenae.

title: The Lernaean hydra
summary: Iolaus sears each neck as Heracles cuts off a head; Eurystheus does not count the labour because Heracles had help.

title: The Ceryneian hind
summary: Heracles hunts the golden-horned hind, sacred to Artemis, for a whole year.

title: The Erymanthian boar
summary: Heracles drives the boar into deep snow and brings it back alive.

title: The stables of Augeas
summary: Heracles cleans the stables in one day by turning the Alpheus and the Peneus through them; Eurystheus does not count it because Augeas promised payment.

title: The Stymphalian birds
summary: Heracles scares the birds from their marsh with bronze clappers made by Hephaestus and given by Athena, then shoots them.

title: The Cretan bull
summary: Heracles brings the bull of Minos to Eurystheus, who lets it go; it roams to Marathon.

title: The mares of Diomedes
summary: Heracles takes the man-eating mares of the Thracian king Diomedes.

title: The belt of Hippolyte
summary: Heracles fetches the belt of the Amazon queen for Eurystheus's daughter Admete.

title: The cattle of Geryon
summary: Heracles crosses the Ocean in the cup of Helios, sets up the Pillars at the strait, kills Orthus and Geryon and drives the cattle to Greece.

title: The apples of the Hesperides
summary: On the way Heracles frees Prometheus; in one account he takes the sky from Atlas while Atlas fetches the apples.

title: Cerberus
summary: With Hades's leave and without weapons, Heracles brings Cerberus up from the underworld and shows him to Eurystheus.

title: The death of Heracles
summary: Deianira sends a robe smeared with the centaur Nessus's poisoned blood, thinking it a love charm; in agony Heracles has himself burned on a pyre on Oeta.

title: Heracles among the gods
summary: Made immortal, Heracles is reconciled with Hera and marries Hebe; Odysseus sees only his image among the dead.
